newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end mixed, SMI hits new closing high.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end mixed, SMI hits new closing high.

text.p: Swiss shares ended mixed as a weaker beginning on Wall Street dampened sentiment, but the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) was still able to finish at a new closing high.
Dealers said the outlook remained unclear given the already high level and U.S. economic data on Wednesday and Thursday.
The SMI eased from a new all-time high of 3,841.9 points set in the second half of the session to end 2.2 points higher, or 0.06 percent, at 3,829.8 points.
All-share SPI ended down 0.64 points at 2,445.74 points.
Volumes were moderate but above Moday's levels, a dealer said. Blue chips such as Nestle, UBS and Zurich saw good demand.
Insurer Zurich posted impressive gains, soaring more than one percent to 358 francs. The stock profited from various buy recommendations and switches, a dealer noted.
Nestle added five francs to 1,420, while UBS bearer shares were up four francs to 1,249. A trader noted the shares saw active buying ahead of a news conference on November 26.

Cyclicals ABB, Alusuisse, Sulzer, Rieter and Georg Fischer posted gains. The record level of the German bourse, which has a high share of cyclical stocks, boosted this segment on the Swiss stock exchange, a dealer said.

Swiss Re slid six francs to 1,377. Monday's news the company wanted to buy Italian reinsurer Unione Italiana di Riassicurazione put off some investors, a trader said. Also, the profit warning by Geman competitor Muenchener Rueck had a negative effect on the stock, a dealer added.
Winterthur and CS Holding were unchanged at 764 francs and 128.50 francs, respectively.

Trade on the Swiss Options and Futures Exchange (Soffex) was lively due to roll-overs in SMI futures ahead of the Soffex expiry on Friday, dealers said. 13,710 SMI futures contracts were traded, 8,585 of which were November contracts and 5,098 December contracts.
